pivots.name: Invitation-based org signup replaces auto-assign
pivots.description: Two migrations (Mar 21) created a trigger that auto-assigned every new signup the project_manager role. Just two days later, both that trigger and function were dropped and replaced with a formal invitations table + accept_invitation() + assign_owner_role() flow. Organic signups now become admin; invited users get the role specified in the invitation token.

pivots.name: Daily report approval locked to Resident Engineer role
pivots.description: The initial daily-report workflow migration included a policy allowing project creators (PMs) to update reports. The very next substantive migration that same day dropped that policy and added a hard check inside the status-transition trigger: only a user with the resident_engineer role who is also a project member may set status to approved or rejected.

pivots.name: Document management replaces flat PDF storage paths
pivots.description: The original schema stored plan/spec PDFs as bare text paths (pdf_storage_path, specs_storage_path) on the projects row. Migration 20260524174837 introduced a full hierarchical document management system (document_folders + documents with versioning), 10 system-seeded folders per project, a non-empty-folder delete guard, and backfilled legacy PDF paths into the Plans/Specs folders.

pivots.name: Schedule calendars + resources additions (P6 parity gap filled)
pivots.description: The first P6-compatible schedule migration (20260526105432) added CPM fields, activity_relationships, and replace_project_schedule() but had no calendar or resource model. Within the same day, migration 20260526115717 added schedule_calendars, schedule_resources, activity_resource_assignments, schedule_baselines/baseline_activities, and upgraded replace_project_schedule() to a 7-argument RPC that atomically imports all of those in one transaction.

pivots.name: demo_requests table isolated — no downstream adoption until RLS hardening
pivots.description: demo_requests was created on 2026-03-28 with a permissive anon INSERT policy. It then had no follow-up migration for two months. The global RLS hardening of 2026-05-28 replaced the permissive INSERT policy with one that validates field lengths and email format — the table's only schema evolution in 36 migrations.

pivots.name: Global RLS hardening and SECURITY DEFINER privilege lock-down
pivots.description: A single migration swept all storage bucket policies (replacing broad authenticated-only checks with project-membership checks), tightened the profiles search policy, added input validation to demo_requests, revoked EXECUTE on all SECURITY DEFINER functions from PUBLIC and anon (trigger-only functions also revoked from authenticated), and enabled RLS on realtime.messages with a project-channel membership gate. This is the most cross-cutting single migration in the timeline.
